# billing ledger census — the INDEPENDENT source for the probe allowlist drift guard.
#
# SOURCE OF TRUTH, not a derivative. This file is the OUTPUT of a query against
# billing_cost_events on the prod postgres primary (worker4). It is NOT generated
# from src/health_probes.py and must never be: a fixture derived from the thing it
# checks can only ever agree with it, and the test reading it would pass against an
# allowlist that had drifted arbitrarily far.
#
# Format, one row per (subject, tenant, service_key, endpoint) tuple:
#   <subject_id>|<tenant_id>|<tenant_name>|<service_key>|<endpoint>|<rows>|<distinct_input_tokens>|<non_internal_transfer_rows>|<modal_input_tokens>
#
# ⚠️ tenant_id is in the key because subject_id ALONE IS NOT AN IDENTITY: the karma
# subject 01a0138e-… serves both svc-kag-karma (the probe) and nonagentic-gtm (real
# traffic, 44 distinct input_tokens) on the SAME service_key and endpoints.
#
# ⚠️ modal_input_tokens is what backs the input_tokens CONJUNCT on each allowlist
# entry. Pinning a payload size makes the rule narrower and safer, but it also makes
# it ROT SILENTLY: change the probe text by one character and the rule stops matching
# while nothing looks wrong. This column is what turns that into a red CI build.
#
# ⚠️ distinct_input_tokens IS EVIDENCE, NOT THE RULE. A triple showing 1 distinct
# value across tens of thousands of rows is almost certainly a probe — but billing
# NEVER keys the exclusion on it. See the '⛔ THE RULE IS KEYED ON IDENTITY' section
# of src/health_probes.py for why a payload-shape rule is the dangerous fix.
#
# Census window: 7 days. Volume floor: 100 rows.
# REFRESH (from a host with tailnet access to worker4):
#     scripts/refresh_health_probe_fixture.sh
# Then run: pytest tests/test_health_probe_exclusion.py
#
